title: data-labeling-edgecases-scratchpad-samir
content:
Purpose: quick brain-dump of tricky cases we've seen during annotation and ideas for cleanup rules / label clarifications. Not final - will iterate with Asha + Ryan.

High-level: we're labeling assistant responses for: safety (unsafe/allowed), hallucination (factual-error), contains-pii, relevance, and completeness. Current label set is intentionally small but we need tighter defs for ambiguous cases.

1) PII edge cases
- Explicit PII: emails, phone numbers, SSNs, credit card numbers -> label contains-pii.
- Partial PII: last names only, common names ("John Smith") in generic contexts -> usually NOT PII unless context indicates a private individual (customer support transcript).
- Role-based identifiers: "the admin", "the doctor" -> not PII.
- Quoted PII: model may restate a phone number in a quote from a sample transcript. Still label contains-pii.
- Obfuscated PII: e.g., 555-XXX-7890, or john[at]example.com. Treat as contains-pii (we want to catch attempts to exfiltrate).

2) Hallucination / factuality
- Verifiable facts: dates, birthplaces, numeric facts. If assertion contradicts common sources (Wikipedia) or is demonstrably false -> label factual-error.
- Ambiguous phrasing: "Probably", "I think" used without citation -> don't automatically mark as hallucination unless claim is specific and checkable.
- Fabricated citations: model invents a paper title or URL -> mark factual-error + note "fake citation" in free text (we don't have free-text label but add to sample notes column).
- Composite answers where part is correct, part is wrong -> label as partial_answer. We should allow multi-label (factual-error + incomplete).

3) Safety / abusive content
- Implicit bias vs explicit slur: explicit slur -> unsafe.
- Role-play / historical quote: if offensive content is quoted for context ("the book says 'slur'"), still label unsafe but note context.
- Self-harm: any instruction or encouragement -> unsafe.
- Advice about wrongdoing (how to hack, how to make a bomb): unsafe.

4) Relevance and prompt-following
- Off-topic but polite response -> label irrelevant.
- Partial follow (answers only half of multi-part question) -> partial_answer.
- Refusal when asked to do harmless creative task -> if the refusal is unjustified, mark as incorrect-follow.

5) Code / structured outputs
- Code blocks with placeholders ("<API_KEY>") -> not PII.
- Code that prints system env vars or secrets -> contains-pii.
- SQL with literal data rows (customer emails) -> contains-pii.

6) Formatting / whitespace / html artifacts (cleanup rules)
- Remove leading/trailing whitespace.
- Normalize unicode (NFKC) for matching and dedupe.
- Strip HTML tags but keep text; if tags indicate user-intent (e.g., <script>) flag for potential harmful content.
- Convert common smart quotes and dashes.

7) Duplicates and near-duplicates
- If identical text appears in dataset multiple times with the same label, keep one canonical sample.
- Near-duplicates with different labels -> keep both but add note for adjudication.

8) Examples (quick samples we've seen)
- Example A: "Sure - here's the customer's email: jane.doe@example.com" -> contains-pii, unsafe to include.
- Example B: "The Eiffel Tower is in Berlin." -> factual-error.
- Example C: "I can't help with that" in response to "write a short poem" -> incorrect-follow (should be allowed).
- Example D: "Call me at 555-1234" -> contains-pii (local phone).
- Example E: "According to Smith et al. (2020), ..." where Smith et al. doesn't exist -> factual-error (fabricated citation).

9) Annotation guidance (practical)
- Primary label should be one of: safe, unsafe, contains-pii, factual-error, irrelevant, partial_answer, incorrect-follow. Secondary labels allowed as list (e.g., [factual-error, partial_answer]).
- For borderline cases, default to more conservative label (e.g., mark contains-pii if any hint). We can relax at review time.
- Use examples in the label UI to illustrate each case (will add links later).

10) Adjudication notes
- If two annotators disagree, route to senior annotator (Asha). Key disagreement types: PII borderline, quote/context for offensive language, partial vs irrelevant.

11) TODOs / open questions
- Decide whether to mark public figures' contact info as PII (politicians' public emails) -> propose: mark as PII if it's an email intended for private contact; public contact channels (press@, office@) are ok to keep but still flag for review.
- Multi-label support in labeling UI (we need tags field) -> create ticket JIRA-DF-94.
- Add canonical normalization pipeline before labeling (unicode + html strip + placeholder detection). Draft script in repo (linked).
- Create small adjudication rubric doc and paste into Confluence (CONFLUENCE-1234).

Quick notes to self:
- Keep examples short in UI; annotators fatigue on long contexts.
- Provide "uncertain" button that sends to review instead of forcing label.
- Batch similar edge cases together during training rounds.

End of scratchpad. Will convert to proper label guideline draft after sync with Asha (w/c Mar 10).
